retainedReference.title: Pashupatinath Temple
retainedReference.reason: No unique physical footprint or centerline with exact Wikidata identity has been resolved.

currentRoundInspection.scope: The specific principal Pashupatinath pagoda exterior: square stone platform, four silver-covered doors in a dark timber lower shrine, two independently mapped gold hipped roofs, the upper timber storey and a tall central gold pinnacle. Courtyard buildings, separate pavilions, river ghats and eastern stone shrines remain independent native context; the broader precinct is not one temple footprint.

pictures.author: Bijay Chaurasia
pictures.observations: Principal shrine has two broad gold-covered hipped roofs with slightly raised eaves, a tall central gold finial, dark carved timber walls and projecting roof struts. The lower roof is considerably broader than the upper. White courtyard buildings and a white eastern gate stand in front; a separate grey-roofed open pavilion is visible southeast of the principal shrine. A nearby article architecture paragraph gives a nominal23.07m height and four silver-covered doors; these are descriptive estimates, not a survey.

pictures.author: Rajesh Dhungana
pictures.observations: Separate stone shrines, red/white buildings, stepped ghats and river occupy the eastern bank. These are surrounding context and must not be mistaken for the gold-roofed principal temple or removed as duplicate main-building geometry. The media GPS caption is inconsistent with the known precinct and is not used for placement.
